examples.en: The children are spinning round and round on the playground.

examples.ko: 놀이기구를 타고 나니 세상이 뱅글뱅글 돌아요.
examples.en: After the ride, the world is spinning around me.
The top spins nicely round and round on the floor.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 같은 자리를 뱅글뱅글 걸으며 전화를 받았어요.
examples.en: He walked round and round the same spot while taking the call.

examples.ko: 머리가 아파서 방이 뱅글뱅글 도는 것 같아요.
examples.en: My head hurts and the room feels like it is spinning.
The puppy spins round and round trying to catch its tail.

explain: '빙글빙글'보다 작고 가벼운 느낌이라 작은 물건이나 아이, 강아지의 움직임에 잘 어울려요. 거의 항상 '돌다'와 함께 쓰고, 어지러울 때 세상이 도는 느낌에도 써요.
explain_en: It feels smaller and lighter than '빙글빙글', so it suits small objects, children and puppies. It is almost always used with '돌다' (to turn), and also for the feeling that the world is spinning when you are dizzy.

examples.en: I am so dizzy that the sky seems to spin.

examples.ko: 같은 곳을 뱅뱅 돌다가 길을 잃었어요.
examples.en: I kept going around the same place and got lost.
A dragonfly is flying around and around above my head.

examples.ko: 강아지가 제 주위를 뱅뱅 돌면서 좋아해요.
examples.en: The puppy circles around me happily.
I am so tired that everything spins before my eyes.
Worries about the exam keep going round and round in my head.

explain: '뱅뱅'은 '돌다'와 가장 자주 함께 써요. 몸이 도는 것뿐 아니라 어지러울 때나 같은 생각이 머릿속에서 계속 맴돌 때도 써요. '빙빙'의 작은 느낌 말이에요.
explain_en: '뱅뱅' goes most often with '돌다' (to turn). It is used for physical spinning, for dizziness, and for a thought that keeps circling in your head. It is the lighter, smaller-feeling counterpart of '빙빙'.

en: come close; be second to the best

examples.ko: 이 식당 음식은 호텔 요리에 버금가요.
examples.en: The food at this restaurant is almost as good as hotel cooking.

examples.ko: 그 선수의 실력은 세계 최고에 버금가요.
examples.en: That player's skill is close to the best in the world.

examples.ko: 우리 동네 도서관은 대학 도서관에 버금가는 규모예요.
examples.en: Our neighborhood library is nearly the size of a university library.

examples.ko: 그 가수의 인기는 아이돌에 버금갈 만큼 대단해요.
examples.en: That singer's popularity is almost on par with an idol's.

examples.ko: 형의 요리 솜씨는 전문가에 버금간다고 다들 말해요.
examples.en: Everyone says my brother's cooking skill rivals a professional's.
This summer's heat was nearly the worst on record.

explain: 보통 '~에 버금가다'처럼 조사 '에'와 함께 써요. 1등 바로 다음 수준이라는 느낌이라 칭찬하거나 수준을 비교할 때 나와요. '비슷하다'보다 격식 있어서 뉴스나 글에서 자주 보여요.
explain_en: It is normally used as '~에 버금가다' with the particle '에'. It means just below the top, so it appears when praising something or comparing levels. It is more formal than '비슷하다' and often seen in news and writing.

examples.en: The child talked back rudely to an adult.
I am really sorry for acting rudely earlier.
I saw a customer behaving rudely in the shop.
My younger sibling shouted disrespectfully at our parents.

examples.ko: 친구라도 선배한테 버릇없이 말하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: Even if you are friends, you shouldn't speak rudely to a senior.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 버릇없이 자랐다고 사람들이 말해요.
examples.en: People say that child was raised without manners.

explain: '버릇없이 굴다/말하다/행동하다'로 자주 써요. 특히 어른이나 윗사람에게 예의 없게 대할 때, 그리고 아이의 행동을 나무랄 때 많이 나와요. 반대로 말할 때는 '예의 바르게'를 써요.
explain_en: It is common in '버릇없이 굴다/말하다/행동하다'. It is used especially when someone is disrespectful to elders or superiors, and when scolding a child's behavior. The opposite is '예의 바르게' (politely).

examples.en: That child felt abandoned by his parents.

examples.ko: 주인에게 버림받아 보호소에 온 강아지를 키우기로 했어요.
examples.en: I decided to raise a puppy that was abandoned by its owner and came to the shelter.
I am always afraid my friends will abandon me.
I cried a lot because the person I loved left me.

examples.ko: 이 영화는 사회에서 버림받은 사람들의 이야기예요.
examples.en: This movie is about people cast out by society.
I try hard so that nobody abandons me.

explain: '누구에게 버림받다'처럼 버린 사람 뒤에 '에게'를 붙여요. 사람뿐 아니라 동물이나 사회에도 써요. 능동은 '버리다'이고, 연인에게 헤어지자는 말을 들은 경우는 일상에서 '차이다'도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: Put '에게' after the person who abandoned you, as in '누구에게 버림받다'. It is used for people, animals and society. The active verb is '버리다', and in daily talk a breakup is often described as '차이다' (to get dumped).

examples.ko: 한복을 입을 때 하얀 버선을 신어요.
examples.en: I wear white beoseon (traditional socks) when I put on hanbok.
My feet were cold, so I took out thick beoseon.
My grandmother made beoseon for me herself.
I looked at old beoseon at the museum.

examples.ko: 버선 끝이 살짝 올라가 있어서 예뻐요.
examples.en: The tip of the beoseon curves up slightly, so they look pretty.

examples.ko: 요즘은 한복 가게에서 버선을 살 수 있어요.
examples.en: These days you can buy beoseon at hanbok shops.

explain: 한복을 입을 때 신는 전통 양말이에요. 요즘 일상에서는 잘 신지 않아서 한복을 입거나 전통 공연을 볼 때 만나요. 일반 '양말'과 달리 발끝이 살짝 위로 휘어 있어요.

phrases.example: 오랜만에 아들이 오자 어머니가 버선발로 뛰어나갔어요.
phrases.en: When her son came after a long time, his mother rushed out in her socks without even putting on shoes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반가운 사람을 맞으려고 신발도 못 신고 급히 나가는 모습을 나타내요. 그만큼 매우 반가워한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It shows someone rushing out without even putting on shoes to greet a welcome person, meaning they are extremely glad to see them.
phrases.en_equiv: rush out to greet someone eagerly

explain_en: Beoseon are the traditional socks worn with hanbok. They are rarely worn in everyday life now, so you meet them with hanbok or traditional performances. Unlike ordinary '양말', the toe tip curves slightly upward.

examples.en: My heart swelled with emotion on graduation day.

examples.ko: 합격 소식을 듣고 감동이 벅차올라서 눈물이 났어요.
examples.en: Hearing I had passed, I was so overcome with emotion that I cried.
Hearing the cheering, joy wells up inside me.

examples.ko: 가슴이 벅차오르는 순간을 오래 기억하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to remember this moment when my heart swells for a long time.

examples.ko: 아이의 첫걸음을 보고 가슴이 벅차오를 만큼 행복했어요.
examples.en: Seeing my child's first steps, I was so happy my heart overflowed.

examples.ko: 이 노래를 들으면 알 수 없는 감정이 벅차올라요.
examples.en: When I hear this song, a feeling I can't name wells up in me.

explain: '가슴이/마음이 벅차오르다'처럼 주로 기쁨이나 감동 같은 좋은 감정에 써요. '오르다'처럼 '올라요, 올랐어요'로 바뀌는 르 불규칙이에요. '북받치다'는 슬픔이나 화처럼 눌렀던 감정이 터질 때도 써요.
explain_en: It is mostly used as '가슴이/마음이 벅차오르다' for good feelings such as joy and being moved. It follows the 르 irregular pattern like '오르다': 올라요, 올랐어요. '북받치다' can also be used for pent-up feelings such as sadness or anger bursting out.

examples.ko: 하늘에서 번갯불이 번쩍하더니 천둥이 크게 쳤어요.
examples.en: Lightning flashed in the sky and then thunder crashed loudly.
A long flash of lightning lit up the night sky.
I took a photo the moment the lightning flashed.
The room brightened for a moment because of the lightning.
He ran off as fast as lightning.

examples.ko: 번갯불을 보고 숫자를 세면 천둥이 얼마나 먼지 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you count after seeing the lightning, you can tell how far away the thunder is.

explain: 일상에서는 '번개'가 훨씬 자주 나와요. '번갯불'은 번개의 빛 자체를 말하는 느낌이고 속담이나 비유에서 자주 만나요. '번갯불처럼'은 아주 빠르다는 비유로 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 무슨 일이든 번갯불에 콩 볶아 먹듯이 해치워요.
phrases.en: He gets any job done in a flash.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행동이 아주 재빠르거나 성격이 매우 급해서 일을 순식간에 해치우는 모습을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: It describes someone so quick or impatient that they finish things in no time.

explain_en: In daily speech '번개' is far more common. '번갯불' focuses on the light of the lightning itself and shows up often in proverbs and figures of speech. '번갯불처럼' is also used to mean extremely fast.

examples.en: Silkworm pupae smell distinctive, but they taste good.
They sell silkworm pupae in paper cups on the street.
A caterpillar becomes a pupa and then turns into a butterfly.
Silkworm pupa soup tastes even better in winter.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 학교 앞에서 번데기를 사 먹었어요.
examples.en: When I was little I bought and ate silkworm pupae in front of school.
I observed a pupa attached to a leaf.

explain: 곤충의 번데기를 가리키기도 하고, 삶은 누에 번데기로 만든 길거리 간식을 가리키기도 해요. 간식은 냄새 때문에 호불호가 갈려요. 속담에서도 가끔 나와요.

phrases.example: 요리사 앞에서 요리법을 가르치다니 번데기 앞에서 주름 잡는 격이에요.
phrases.en: Teaching a chef how to cook is like showing off in front of an expert.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잘 아는 사람 앞에서 아는 척하며 나서는 것을 놀리듯 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said teasingly when someone shows off in front of a person who knows far more.
phrases.en_equiv: teach your grandmother to suck eggs

explain_en: It means the pupa stage of an insect and also the street snack made of boiled silkworm pupae. The snack divides people because of its smell. It also appears occasionally in proverbs.

examples.en: If you tell me the lot number, I will come find it.
The address is right, but the lot number is wrong.
What is this building's lot number?
You have to write the lot number exactly for the letter to arrive.

examples.ko: 요즘은 번지수 대신 도로명 주소를 써요.
examples.en: These days we use road-name addresses instead of lot numbers.

examples.ko: 약속 장소를 번지수까지 정확히 알려 줬어요.
examples.en: He told me the meeting place right down to the lot number.

explain: 예전 주소 체계의 '번지'를 가리켜요. 지금은 도로명 주소가 공식이라서 일상에서는 오히려 비유로 더 많이 나와요. 아래 표현은 말하는 사람이 대상을 잘못 골랐을 때 써요.

phrases.example: 화낼 상대가 아닌데 번지수를 잘못 짚으셨어요.
phrases.en: I'm not the one you should be angry at; you've got the wrong person.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문제의 원인이나 말을 건넬 대상을 잘못 잡았을 때 써요. 상대의 실수를 가볍게 지적하는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone has picked the wrong cause or the wrong target. It is a light way of pointing out a mistake.

explain_en: It refers to the lot number ('번지') of the older address system. Road-name addresses are now official, so in daily speech it appears more often in a figurative phrase. The expression below is used when someone targets the wrong person or thing.

examples.en: Lightning kept flashing in the night sky.
I polished my shoes until they gleamed.

examples.ko: 차 위에서 햇빛이 번쩍거려서 눈이 부셨어요.
examples.en: Sunlight flashed off the car and dazzled my eyes.

examples.ko: 번쩍거리는 불빛 때문에 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: I couldn't sleep because of the flashing lights.
His gold necklace glitters.
A police car's lights are flashing in the distance.

explain: '번쩍이다'와 거의 같게 쓰는데, 빛이 계속 되풀이해서 나는 느낌이 있어요. '반짝거리다'보다 빛이 더 크고 강해요. 번개, 불빛, 윤이 나는 물건에 잘 써요.
explain_en: It is used almost the same as '번쩍이다', with a sense of light flashing repeatedly. The light is bigger and stronger than with '반짝거리다'. It suits lightning, flashing lights and shiny objects.

examples.en: Lightning flashed and soon the rain poured down.

examples.ko: 어두운 방에서 휴대폰 화면이 번쩍여서 잠이 깼어요.
examples.en: The phone screen flashed in the dark room and woke me up.
A light flashed right in front of me and startled me.
My new watch glitters in the sunlight.

examples.ko: 카메라 플래시가 번쩍이는 순간 눈을 감았어요.
examples.en: I closed my eyes the moment the camera flash went off.
The child's eyes lit up with curiosity.

explain: 번개나 플래시처럼 순간적으로 강하게 빛나는 것에 써요. '번쩍거리다'와 거의 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요. 눈이 '번쩍 뜨이다'처럼 '번쩍'만 따로 쓰는 표현도 많아요.
explain_en: It is used for things that flash strongly for a moment, such as lightning or a camera flash. It can almost always be swapped with '번쩍거리다'. The bare '번쩍' also appears in set expressions such as '눈이 번쩍 뜨이다' (eyes snap open).

examples.en: I was so embarrassed that my face turned red.

examples.ko: 매운 걸 먹으면 얼굴이 금방 벌게져요.
examples.en: My face quickly turns red when I eat spicy food.

examples.ko: 추운 날 밖에 있었더니 코가 벌게졌어요.
examples.en: I was outside on a cold day and my nose turned red.

examples.ko: 화가 나서 귀까지 벌게진 채 소리쳤어요.
examples.en: He shouted with his ears red with anger.

examples.ko: 햇볕에 오래 있었더니 팔이 벌게져서 따가워요.
examples.en: I was in the sun for a long time and my arm is red and stinging.
I cried for a long time until my eyes were red.

explain: 부끄러움, 화, 추위, 햇볕 때문에 얼굴이나 피부가 붉어질 때 써요. '빨개지다'보다 어둡고 탁한 붉은색 느낌이에요. '벌겋다'가 기본형 형용사이고 '벌게지다'는 그렇게 변하는 과정을 말해요.
explain_en: It is used when the face or skin turns red from embarrassment, anger, cold or sun. The red feels darker and duller than with '빨개지다'. '벌겋다' is the adjective, and '벌게지다' describes the change into that color.

examples.en: That company brought in a lot of money last year.
It is a country that earns foreign currency through exports.
How much does the shop bring in per day these days?

examples.ko: 이 가게가 한 해에 벌어들인 돈이 꽤 많대요.
examples.en: I heard this shop earned quite a lot in a year.

examples.ko: 이 나라는 수출로 더 많은 돈을 벌어들여야 해요.
examples.en: This country has to earn more money through exports.

examples.ko: 그 가게는 연휴에 돈을 더 벌어들이려고 밤늦게까지 문을 열었어요.
examples.en: That shop stayed open late to bring in more money during the holiday.

explain: '벌다'보다 돈을 안으로 끌어오는 느낌이 강하고, 회사·나라·가게 이야기에 많이 나와요. 개인이 용돈이나 월급을 번다고 할 때는 그냥 '벌다'가 훨씬 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It has a stronger sense of bringing money in than plain '벌다', and it is common when talking about companies, countries and shops. For an individual earning pocket money or a salary, plain '벌다' is far more natural.

examples.en: This neighborhood has a low crime rate, so it's safe.
The crime rate is dropping a little every year.
The crime rate differs a lot from city to city.
I heard the crime rate fell after more streetlights were added.
The news said the youth crime rate has gone up.
What should we do to lower the crime rate?

explain: '높다/낮다', '늘다/줄다', '오르다/떨어지다'와 함께 써요. '실업률', '출산율'처럼 통계를 말할 때 붙는 '-률/-율'이에요. 뉴스와 토론 글에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It goes with '높다/낮다' (high/low), '늘다/줄다' (increase/decrease) and '오르다/떨어지다' (rise/fall). The ending '-률/-율' is the same one in '실업률' and '출산율', used for statistics. It appears often in news and debate writing.

examples.en: I paid a fine for driving while looking at my phone.
How much is the speeding fine on this road?
The fine notice came to my house.
You get a fine if you don't wear your seat belt.
You must pay the fine within the deadline.
I ran a light on my motorcycle and had to pay a fine.

explain: 주로 교통법규를 어겼을 때 내는 돈이에요. '범칙금을 내다/물다/부과받다'로 써요. 비슷한 '과태료', '벌금'이 있지만 제도가 서로 달라서 같은 말은 아니에요.
explain_en: It is mainly the money you pay for breaking traffic rules, used as '범칙금을 내다/물다/부과받다'. There are similar words, '과태료' and '벌금', but they belong to different systems, so they are not the same thing.

examples.en: As soon as I got home, I flung off my coat.
It's so hot that I want to throw off my coat.
Now try to shake off your old prejudices.
The child kicked off his shoes and ran to the sea.

examples.ko: 그는 체면을 벗어던진 채 춤을 췄어요.
examples.en: He cast aside his dignity and danced.
Don't just fling your socks off; put them in the laundry basket.

explain: 옷이나 신발을 거칠게 벗어 던질 때도 쓰고, 편견·체면·걱정 같은 추상적인 것을 떨쳐 버릴 때도 써요. 그냥 '벗다'보다 힘 있고 시원한 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It is used for taking off clothes or shoes roughly and tossing them aside, and also for shaking off abstract things such as prejudice, dignity or worries. It feels more forceful and liberating than plain '벗다'.

examples.en: The child smiles broadly after getting a present.
My younger sibling is beaming after seeing the test score.
My father has been smiling happily since morning.
The baby saw its mother and smiled broadly.

examples.ko: 뭐가 그렇게 좋아서 혼자 벙글벙글 웃어요?
examples.en: What makes you so happy that you are grinning to yourself?
The whole family was beaming at the news of the acceptance.

explain: 소리 없이 기분 좋게 환하게 웃는 모습에 써요. '벙글벙글 웃다/하다' 형태로 자주 나와요. '싱글벙글'도 거의 같은 뜻으로 일상에서 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It describes smiling brightly and happily without much sound, often as '벙글벙글 웃다/하다'. '싱글벙글' is used in much the same way and is very common in daily speech.

examples.ko: 쿠키를 만들 때 베이킹파우더를 한 숟갈 넣어요.
examples.en: When I make cookies, I add a spoonful of baking powder.

examples.ko: 베이킹파우더가 없으면 빵이 잘 부풀지 않아요.
examples.en: Without baking powder, the bread doesn't rise well.
I bought baking powder and flour at the supermarket.
I store baking powder in a place without moisture.

examples.ko: 팬케이크 반죽에 베이킹파우더를 너무 많이 넣지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't put too much baking powder in the pancake batter.
Baking powder and baking soda are different from each other.

explain: 빵이나 케이크 반죽을 부풀리는 가루예요. '베이킹소다'와 이름이 비슷하지만 다른 재료라서 레시피에서 바꿔 쓰면 안 돼요. 요리 레시피에서는 '베이킹파우더 1작은술'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is the powder that makes bread and cake batter rise. The name is similar to '베이킹소다' (baking soda), but they are different ingredients and should not be swapped in a recipe. Recipes write it like '베이킹파우더 1작은술' (1 teaspoon).

examples.en: The child read the story of the ant and the grasshopper.

examples.ko: 여름 내내 노래만 부른 베짱이는 겨울에 배가 고팠어요.
examples.en: The grasshopper that only sang all summer was hungry in winter.

examples.ko: 일은 안 하고 놀기만 하는 사람을 베짱이라고 불러요.
examples.en: People call someone who only plays and doesn't work a 'grasshopper'.
I hear grasshoppers from the bushes every night.
The child fell asleep holding a grasshopper doll.

examples.ko: 저도 베짱이처럼 살고 싶지만 그럴 수 없어요.
examples.en: I'd like to live like a grasshopper too, but I can't.

explain: 곤충 이름이지만 '개미와 베짱이' 이야기로 가장 많이 알려져 있어요. 그래서 놀기만 하고 일하지 않는 사람을 가볍게 놀리듯 비유할 때도 써요. 반대로 부지런한 사람은 '개미'에 비유해요.
explain_en: It is an insect, but it is best known from the story '개미와 베짱이' (The Ant and the Grasshopper). So it is also used playfully for someone who only plays and doesn't work. A hard worker is compared to an '개미' (ant).

examples.en: Please put the bedding inside the built-in closet.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 벽장 속에 숨어서 놀았어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I played hiding inside the closet.
I found an old album in the closet.
Our house has a built-in closet in every room.
I put the winter clothes away in the closet.
The closet door doesn't close well.

explain: 벽 안쪽에 붙박이로 만든 수납 공간이에요. 따로 놓는 가구인 '장롱'이나 '옷장'과 달리 벽에 붙어 있어요. 요즘 아파트에서는 '붙박이장'이라는 말도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is a storage space built into a wall. Unlike freestanding furniture such as '장롱' or '옷장', it is part of the wall. In modern apartments people also say '붙박이장' (built-in wardrobe).

examples.ko: 그 친구는 변덕쟁이라서 약속을 자주 바꿔요.
examples.en: That friend is fickle, so he often changes plans.
Today's weather seems fickle.
I'm so fickle that I keep changing my order.

examples.ko: 변덕쟁이 고양이가 안으면 싫어하고 내려놓으면 따라와요.
examples.en: The fickle cat dislikes being held but follows you when you put it down.

examples.ko: 동생이 변덕쟁이여서 여행 계획 짜기가 힘들어요.
examples.en: My sibling is so fickle that planning a trip is hard.
Don't be so fickle; just pick one.

explain: '-쟁이'는 어떤 특징이 강한 사람에게 붙어서 약간 놀리는 느낌이 있어요. 윗사람이나 친하지 않은 사람 앞에서 직접 말하면 무례할 수 있어요. 부드럽게 말하려면 '변덕스럽다'를 쓰고, 날씨에도 '날씨가 변덕스럽다'고 해요.
explain_en: The suffix '-쟁이' attaches to people with a strong trait and carries a slightly teasing tone. Saying it directly to a superior or someone you aren't close to can be rude. For a softer way, use the adjective '변덕스럽다', which is also used for weather.

examples.ko: 그 사람이 변심하는 바람에 계약이 취소됐어요.
examples.en: The contract was canceled because he changed his mind.
The customer changed their mind and asked for a refund.
I realized the person I love had a change of heart.

examples.ko: 그 사람이 변심한 이유를 알고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to know why he changed his mind.

examples.ko: 단순 변심이라도 일주일 안에는 환불이 돼요.
examples.en: Even a simple change of mind can get a refund within a week.
I'm worried my friend will change his mind.

explain: 연인의 마음이 변했을 때, 그리고 사려던 사람이 마음을 바꿨을 때 모두 써요. 쇼핑에서는 '단순 변심'이 반품·환불 이유로 자주 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '마음이 변하다'라고 더 흔히 말해요.
explain_en: It is used both when a lover's feelings change and when a buyer changes their mind. In shopping, '단순 변심' (simple change of mind) often appears as a reason for returns and refunds. In daily conversation people more commonly say '마음이 변하다'.

examples.ko: 눈치가 빠르니까 별말 안 해도 알아서 도와주더라고요.
examples.en: She's quick on the uptake, so she helps on her own without being told much.
He just nodded without saying anything in particular.

examples.ko: 회의에서 별말이 안 나와서 일찍 끝났어요.
examples.en: Nothing much came up in the meeting, so it ended early.

examples.ko: 친구가 별말도 안 했는데 제가 괜히 서운했어요.
examples.en: My friend hadn't said anything special, but I felt hurt for no reason.

examples.ko: 오랜만에 만났는데 별말 없이 밥만 먹었어요.
examples.en: We met after a long time but just ate without much talk.
The child didn't say anything much even after being scolded.

explain: 거의 '별말 없다/안 하다'처럼 부정하는 말과 함께 써요. 특별히 할 말이 없거나 따로 말하지 않았다는 느낌이에요. 높임말 '별말씀'은 상대가 고맙다고 하거나 사과할 때 겸손하게 대답하는 인사로 많이 써요.

phrases.example: A: 도와주셔서 정말 감사해요. B: 별말씀을요.
phrases.en: A: Thank you so much for helping. B: Not at all.
phrases.nuance_ko: 감사나 사과를 받았을 때 '그럴 필요 없다'는 뜻으로 겸손하게 답하는 말이에요. 윗사람에게도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modest reply to thanks or an apology, meaning there is no need. It can be used with superiors too.

explain_en: It is almost always used with a negative, as in '별말 없다/안 하다', meaning nothing in particular was said. The honorific form '별말씀' is a very common modest reply when someone thanks you or apologizes.

examples.en: They said the test results showed no particular problem.

examples.ko: 이 정도 비라면 행사에 별문제 없을 거예요.
examples.en: With rain this light, there should be no real problem for the event.
I hope no particular problem occurs with the machine.
It's not a big deal, so don't worry too much.

examples.ko: 처음에는 별문제 없다가 나중에 고장이 났어요.
examples.en: At first there was no problem, but later it broke down.

examples.ko: 대화해 보니 그 사람에게 별문제가 있는 것 같지는 않았어요.
examples.en: After talking, it didn't seem like anything was particularly wrong with him.

explain: 거의 '별문제 없다/아니다'처럼 부정하는 말과 함께 써요. 큰 문제가 없다고 안심시킬 때 자주 나와요. 안부를 물을 때는 '별일 없어요?'라고 하는 것이 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It is almost always used with a negative, as in '별문제 없다/아니다', often to reassure someone that nothing serious is wrong. When asking how someone is doing, '별일 없어요?' is the natural phrase.

en: particularly good taste; food with particularly good taste

examples.en: In this region, oyster pancakes are the winter specialty.
Cold noodles are a summer treat.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날 김치전은 최고의 별미 같아요.
examples.en: On a rainy day, kimchi pancakes feel like the best treat.

examples.ko: 여행 가면 그 지역 별미를 꼭 먹어 봐요.
examples.en: When I travel, I always try the local specialty.
Even cup noodles are a treat when I eat them once in a while.

examples.ko: 별미로 먹는 간식이라 평소엔 안 만들어요.
examples.en: It's a snack for special occasions, so I don't usually make it.

explain: 평소에 먹는 밥이 아니라 특별히 맛있게 느껴지는 음식에 써요. 그 계절이나 그 지역에서만 맛볼 수 있는 음식에도 자주 써요. '별식'(특별한 음식)과도 가까운 말이에요.
explain_en: It refers to food that tastes especially good compared with everyday meals, and it is often used for seasonal or regional dishes. It is close in meaning to '별식' (a special dish).

examples.ko: 이제 와서 별수 없으니 그냥 기다려요.
examples.en: There's nothing else we can do now, so let's just wait.

examples.ko: 길이 막혀서 별수 없이 중간에 내려 걸었어요.
examples.en: The road was jammed, so I had no choice but to get off midway and walk.
No matter how I think about it, there's no other way.

examples.ko: 제가 별수 있겠어요, 시키는 대로 해야 해요.
examples.en: What else can I do? I have to do as I'm told.

examples.ko: 그 사람도 별수 없는 평범한 사람이에요.
examples.en: He is just an ordinary person, no different from anyone else.

examples.ko: 아무리 애써도 별수 없다는 걸 알았어요.
examples.en: I realized that no matter how hard I try, there's nothing to be done.

explain: 거의 '별수 없다/있다'로만 써요. '어쩔 수 없다'와 비슷하게 다른 방법이 없다는 뜻이에요. '별수 없는 사람'처럼 남들과 다를 게 없다는 뜻으로도 써요.
explain_en: It is used almost only as '별수 없다/있다'. Like '어쩔 수 없다', it means there is no other way. In '별수 없는 사람' it also means a person no different from anyone else.

examples.en: I took leave to take care of my mother during her illness.

examples.ko: 며칠째 병간호를 하느라 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: I haven't slept for days because I've been nursing someone.
Nursing a patient is hard on the family.
My father was hospitalized, so my older sister took charge of his care.

examples.ko: 병간호에 지친 가족을 위해 간병인을 구했어요.
examples.en: We hired a caregiver for the family worn out from nursing.
After a long period of nursing, my grandmother recovered.

explain: '병간호를 하다/맡다'처럼 써요. 가족이 아픈 사람을 곁에서 돌보는 일에 많이 쓰고, 직업으로 하는 사람은 '간병인'이라고 해요. 동사로는 '간호하다'나 '돌보다'도 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It is used as '병간호를 하다/맡다', most often for family members looking after a sick person. A professional who does this is called a '간병인'. As verbs, '간호하다' and '돌보다' are also common.

examples.ko: 손을 씻으면 병균을 막을 수 있어요.
examples.en: Washing your hands can keep germs away.
Spoiled food has a lot of germs.
I wore a mask so that germs wouldn't spread.
Children tend to be vulnerable to germs.
I got rid of the kitchen germs with disinfectant.
Germs can't be seen with the eyes.

explain: 병을 일으키는 작은 생물을 두루 가리키는 말이에요. 일상에서는 '세균', '균', '바이러스'도 많이 쓰는데, 세균과 바이러스는 과학적으로 서로 달라요. '병균'은 그런 구분 없이 '병을 옮기는 것'으로 쉽게 말할 때 편해요.
explain_en: It broadly refers to tiny organisms that cause disease. In daily life '세균', '균' and '바이러스' are also used, though bacteria and viruses are scientifically different. '병균' is handy when you just mean something that spreads illness, without making that distinction.
